methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: Guest column highlighting small-business adoption lag signals that while data center infrastructure concentrates in NoVA, practical AI capability remains shallow and unevenly distributed across Virginia's business ecosystem—neither depth nor breadth materializing outside tech hubs.

signals.title: New details emerge about Botetourt grid upgrades for Google data center
signals.signal_reading: Google's $264M grid infrastructure investment in Botetourt concentrates deep AI compute capability in Southwest Virginia, but as datacenter infrastructure rather than distributed workforce capability—creating geographic pockets of technical excellence without necessarily building local AI fluency.

signals.title: Israeli AI maritime tech company joins Virginia Beach incubator - The Virginian-Pilot
signals.signal_reading: Israeli maritime AI firm joining Virginia Beach incubator signals Hampton Roads developing specialized domain expertise around defense/maritime AI applications, creating a concentrated pocket of deep capability distinct from NoVA's general tech concentration.

signals.title: Loudoun to consider data center pause, removing by-right grandfather clause
signals.signal_reading: Loudoun considering data center pause with grandfather clause removal indicates even the most concentrated AI infrastructure region confronting limits to expansion—potentially forcing some distribution of future capability to other Virginia regions.

signals.title: 6 things to know about the Wood Haven deal that we otherwise don’t know much about
signals.signal_reading: Community engagement and transparency questions around Wood Haven Technology Park data center deal in Roanoke signals potential for distributed civic capacity-building—local stakeholders developing fluency to negotiate tech development rather than passively receiving it.
